walkthroughs.body_html: Of the around 400 Mt produced each year, roughly 9 percent is recycled, 19 percent incinerated and 50 percent landfilled, leaving about 22 percent mismanaged. Around 11 Mt per year leak into oceans. UK per capita plastic waste is around 99 kg per year. Tracking these flows uses mass-balance accounting like a national budget.

Recycling rate = (mass recycled / mass generated) x 100. If 500 kg of bottles are collected and 350 kg recycled, the rate is 70 percent. UK packaging recycling targets aim for 65 percent overall by 2025. Contamination, mixed polymers and food residue reduce real-world recycling rates and create downcycling rather than true closed loops.

DRS charges a small deposit (e.g. 20p) on bottles, refunded on return. Germany's scheme achieves around 98 percent return rates. Scotland is rolling one out; England and Wales plan one for 2027. DRS cuts litter, increases clean recyclate, and shifts cost to producers. Combined with bans on items like cotton bud sticks and straws, it tackles macroplastic flows.
